newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up on one buyer, but backdrop bullish.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up on one buyer, but backdrop bullish.

text.p: May Brent crude futures were firmer in late afternoon trading on SIMEX, largely supported by one player pushing prices higher during small volume trading, brokers said.
May Brent was last traded at $20.35 per barrel on just 85 lots, up 17 cents from London overnight. The contract earlier traded as high as $20.48.
"It looks like someone is trying to high tick the market on low volume," one broker said. "It's the same as what happened to ACCESS earlier in the week."
However, one broker also said there was some news bubbling under the market, which could offer support, but not an immediate buying rush.
He referred to the fuel crisis in Nigeria. He said also there was talk of fuel shortages in the domestic Algerian market.

Another broker said fund interest could be switching more to commodities because of worries U.S. stock markets could be on the verge of a major correction, which would undermine stock markets elsewhere.
